subject: Left-Censored data with differing censoring points per group.

messages.author: 01a98a9cde9cc3be
messages.subject: Left-Censored data with differing censoring points per group.
parts:
I'm having trouble figuring out how to proceed with this model. 

It's a linear hierarchical model with responses that are left censored at a value that varies between groups.


y ~ N(P + G, s)
P ~ N(mu_p, sigma_p)
G ~ N(mu_g, sigma_g)

Within each group, only the response for the top 30 products are reported, so unreported responses are left censored at min(Group response). Just setting an upper limit on the censored response doesn't work because you can't use vectors for the limits. I can't find similar example by searching or in the manual, so I could really use some help.


data {
  int<lower=0> N_ucs; // number of uncensored observations
  int<lower=0> N_cs; // number of censored observations

  int<lower=0> N_pid; // number of products
  int<lower=0> N_gid; // number of groups
  
  int<lower=0> pid_ucs[N_ucs]; //product id (uncensored)
  int<lower=0> pid_cs[N_cs]; //product id (censored)
  
  vector<lower=0>[N_ucs] y; // observed response
  real<lower=0> U[N_cs]; // upper limit for censored response
  
  int<lower=0> gid_ucs[N_ucs]; //group id (uncensored)
  int<lower=0> gid_cs[N_cs]; //group id (censored)
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> pid_beta[N_pid]; // product effect
  real<lower=0> pid_mu;
  real<lower=0> pid_sigma;
  
  real sid_beta[N_gid]; // group effect
  real<lower=0> gid_mu;
  real<lower=0> gid_sigma;
  
  real<lower=0> y_sigma; //regression variance
  
  real<lower=0, upper=U> y_cs[N_cs]; // estimates for censored response
}

transformed parameters{
  vector[N_ucs] mu_ucs;
  vector[N_cs] mu_cs;

  for(n in 1:N_ucs) mu_ucs[n] <-pid_beta[pid_ucs[n]] + gid_beta[gid_ucs[n]];
  for(n in 1:N_cs) mu_cs[n] <- pid_beta[pid_cs[n]] + gid_beta[gid_cs[n]];
}

model {
  // Priors
  y_sigma~inv_gamma(0.1,0.1);
  pid_mu ~ normal(300, 100);
  pid_sigma ~ inv_gamma(0.1,0.1);
  gid_mu ~ normal(-300, 100);
  gid_sigma ~ inv_gamma(0.1,0.1);
  
  // Pooled Priors
  pid_beta ~ normal(pid_mu, pid_sigma);
  gid_beta ~ normal(gid_mu, gid_sigma);
  
  // Likelihood
  y_ucs ~ normal(mu_ucs, y_sigma);
  y_cs ~ normal(mu_cs, y_sigma);
}

messages.subject: Re: Left-Censored data with differing censoring points per group.
parts:
Ok, I've got it to compile by dropping y_cs from parameters, and replacing y_cs likelihood with:

  increment_log_prob(normal_cdf_log(U, mu_cs, y_sigma));

(not sure if this is correct though!)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Left-Censored data with differing censoring points per group.
parts:
The truncated distributions are not vectorized. But you could
do something like:

for (n in 1:N_cs)
y_cs ~ normal(mu_cs, y_sigma) T[0,U];

You've already declared y_cs with the appropriate constraint, which
is the critical part:
real<lower=0, upper=U> y_cs[N_cs]; // estimates for censored response

So note that you are also truncating below at L=0, so that also needs
to be rolled in.

I don't think there's an easy way to vectorize all of this and still
get the lower and upper truncations right. That's why we didn't build
it in. If you unfold the density, what you have is this:

Normal(z | mu, sigma) T[L,U]

=def= Normal(z | mu,sigma)
---------------------------------------------
NormalCDF(U | mu,sigma) - NormalCDF(0 | mu,sigma)

and the problem with putting this on the log scale is that the
difference of CDFS is on the linear scale, whereas the result needs
to be on the log scale. You can do it yourself and perhaps save a bit
of efficiency, but I think it'd be a lot easier to understand just
written using the truncation.

- Bob
